prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the mortgage-underwriting agent (residential mortgage applications and remortgages) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: flood and the mortgage valuation. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 1)
response: {"items":[{"type":"observation","content":"When the valuation report flags a flood risk, I check whether the concern is about the home’s marketability, insurability or both, because those are separate underwriting questions and each can affect the case differently."},{"type":"fact","content":"When flood risk appears in a valuation, I look for evidence that buildings insurance is available on standard terms or with a workable excess, because a mortgage can be harder to proceed with if insurance is not realistically obtainable."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the valuation mentions a past flood event, I do not treat the event alone as decisive; I compare the date, depth, source and any remedial works so I can judge the current risk more accurately."},{"type":"preference","content":"When the valuer gives a plain-language comment rather than a technical flood classification, I prefer to request clarification early rather than guess, because vague wording can hide whether the issue is minor, moderate or serious."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the property is near a watercourse, I pay attention to whether the valuation notes elevated ground, flood defences or drainage improvements, since local mitigation can change the practical underwriting position."},{"type":"fact","content":"When a valuation indicates repeated flooding or credible evidence of recurring water ingress, I treat that as a stronger concern than a one-off historical incident, because repeat events usually point to a persistent exposure."},{"type":"observation","content":"When a remortgage valuation is more conservative than an earlier purchase valuation, I check whether flood risk has changed or whether the valuer is simply applying a stricter view of the same location."},{"type":"preference","content":"When there is any doubt about flood mapping versus on-site observations, I prefer to rely on the valuation report and any supporting survey details together, rather than on mapping alone, because desk-based data can miss property-specific features."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the valuation notes that flood risk may affect future saleability, I consider whether the loan term and product choice still make sense, because marketability risk can matter as much as immediate physical damage risk."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the valuation highlights flood exposure but the case is otherwise strong, I look for proportionate ways forward, such as conditions, evidence requests or referral, rather than an automatic decline."}]}
